models_evaluated: two-phase LLM framework (instruction fine-tuning + confidence-regularization fine-tuning)
baseline LLM with few-shot in-context learning

links.outcome: Calibration (ECE, Brier score, average confidence) after confidence-regularization fine-tuning for feature extraction
links.effect: ECE rose from 0.060 to 0.147 while Brier score improved from 0.087 to 0.036; average confidence stayed at 0.84 (SD 0.003) as F1 rose from 0.819 to 0.986.
links.quote: Calibration evaluation on few-shot training (100 patient notes) showed that the expected calibration error increased from 0.060 to 0.147, whereas the Brier score improved from 0.087 to 0.036.

unlisted_practices: Confidence-regularization fine-tuning with loss penalizing overconfident incorrect predictions
Bidirectional matching to detect hallucinated and missing features
Inference-time confidence filtering of extracted features
Few-shot fine-tuning with limited labeled data

screen.reason: The study develops and benchmarks a two-phase LLM training framework (instruction tuning + confidence-regularized fine-tuning) for medical feature extraction to reduce hallucinations on a standard examination dataset. It does not test an organizational deployment practice or operational safeguard.
